newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat's aides call Israeli offer a trick.
newsitem.headline: Arafat's aides call Israeli offer a trick.

text.p: Aides to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Thursday slammed Israel's offer to finish making peace in six months as a trick and publicity stunt aimed at scrapping existing accords and dodging world criticism.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had proposed bypassing three interim Israeli troop withdrawals from the West Bank to complete "final status" talks within six months, nearly two years earlier than planned, political sources said on Wednesday.
"It's not at all a serious proposal," said Arafat's adviser Ahmed Tibi. "We are speaking of a publicity stunt.
"This is a strategic proposal whose aim is to wipe out the interim agreement completely," he told Israel Radio.

PLO officials said they had not been officially informed of the proposal but knew about it. They accused Netanyahu of trying to duck condemnation of the groundbreaking this week on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

An Israeli source said Netanyahu made the offer because the Oslo interim peace accords, which commit Israel to the three pullbacks in parallel with talks on the fate of the occupied West Bank and Gaza, "created confrontations".
Netanyahu's office declined comment on the plan.
But Yaacov Bardugo, Israeli coordinator of peace talks in the foreign ministry, defended the proposal on Thursday.

"In abnormal situations, abnormal things must be done...It's a modern, creative additional thing...It's a new creation that the prime minister, defence minister and foreign minister are creating within the process," he told Channel 2 Television.
Arafat was due to travel on Thursday to Cairo for talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on the peace crisis.

Netanyahu's office confirmed he had spoken to Mubarak on Wednesday night. A spokeswoman said the Israeli leader would likely send his foriegn policy adviser Dore Gold and perhaps a foreign ministry official to meet Mubarak on Thursday.

Addressing the Israeli plan, chief PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters: "It's a new trick from Netanyahu and an attempt to divert people's attention from the destruction of the peace process that is taking place by Israeli bulldozers on Jabal Abu Ghneim."

Israeli tractors this week began work at Jabal Abu Ghneim, a pine-covered hill occupied in 1967, drawing criticism from allies and prompting fears of violence. The hill is known as Har Homa in Hebrew.

"Netanyahu informed (Jordan's) King Hussein that he wants to jump over the interim period and move directly into permanent status talks. The PLO was informed by King Hussein," a PLO official told Reuters.

Erekat insisted Israel stick to an original timetable to pull its troops out of West Bank rural areas by mid-1998 in tandem with the final status talks due to have resumed this week and end by May 1999.
"There is no contradiction between going with permanent status negotiations and continuing with implementation of the outstanding commitments of the interim agreement," he said.
Final status talks will tackle the thorniest issues dividing Israel and the Palestinians, including borders, Jewish settlements, refugees and Jerusalem.
